observation_summary: The Closure Compiler incorrectly reports a type mismatch error when passing an object literal to a function, claiming a property is (string|undefined) when it is explicitly defined as string. This behavior is triggered by unrelated code elsewhere in the file, suggesting an issue in the type inference or checking algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The bug involves the compiler's type-checking algorithm incorrectly inferring or merging types across unrelated functions. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler tracks and validates object property types during type checking, rather than a missing guard (Checking), a simple initialization error (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).

evidence_gaps: The specific internal type-checking logic (e.g., TypeInference.java or similar) is not provided in the snippets, requiring inference of the root cause from the reported behavior.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the bug involves cross-cutting associations between unrelated functions, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the type inference algorithm that fails to correctly isolate these scopes.
The error is not a missing guard, but an incorrect result from the type-checking logic itself.
